newsitem.title: ITALY: Eat greens to end world hunger, says giant carrot.
newsitem.headline: Eat greens to end world hunger, says giant carrot.

text.p: An Italian dressed as a vivid orange carrot paraded on Rome's ancient Capitoline Hill on Thursday carrying a message for world leaders at a nearby food summit -- "Don't eat meat!"
The seven-foot-high (two metres) "Chris P. Carrot" drew bemused glances from tourists admiring Michelangelo's 16th century palace on Piazza Campidoglio.
He toured the square bearing placards declaring "Eat your veggies, not your friends" and "Life for All."
A United Nations-sponsored World Food Summit taking place in the Italian capital has pledged to halve the number of hungry people in the world in 20 years.

"We want people to go vegetarian," said organiser Toni Vernelli of U.S.-based People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals. "A plot of land can feed 12 people who eat vegetables and grains but only one person who eats meat."
